requirements.requirement: node2's inventory application log messages are forwarded to a centralized log collector on node1
requirements.summary: node2 runs inventory.service emitting syslog-tagged 'inventory' messages; rsyslog on node2 forwards programname=inventory via omfwd TCP to node1:514 with a persistent queue. node1 runs imtcp on 514/tcp with firewalld permanently opened. A test message logged via `logger -t inventory` on node2 appeared on node1 within seconds, and steady 10s-interval 'tick' messages also arrived, demonstrating live end-to-end forwarding.

requirements.requirement: Received messages are persisted on node1 under /var/log/inventory/node2.log
requirements.summary: rsyslog on node1 matches fromhost-ip/programname and writes to /var/log/inventory/node2.log via omfile; directory and file exist with correct content matching forwarded inventory messages.

requirements.requirement: Log flow continues working after node1 restarts
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id, active rsyslog, listening 514, existing log content) at cmd-732b88708481470e; reboot acknowledged at cmd-1db13849d6504d1c; new boot_id confirmed distinct at cmd-6dfb19f6c22540e9; recovery shown via active rsyslog, relistening 514/tcp, and persisted firewall rule at cmd-dfe742d785da4962; new inventory messages generated on node2 post-node1-reboot and observed appended to /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1 at cmd-909ea748bba94662 and cmd-e66d022f38cc4895, confirming a full bounded disruption-and-recovery transition.

requirements.requirement: Log flow continues working after node2 restarts
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline (boot_id, active rsyslog+inventory.service) captured at cmd-0e4dc70d47cd41a9; reboot acknowledged at cmd-e5dbe7e885614b69; distinct post-reboot boot_id confirmed at cmd-202ea1e292574321; recovery shown via active rsyslog+inventory.service and freshly generated tick messages on node2 at cmd-a4eab49a135a4631, which were observed appended to node1's /var/log/inventory/node2.log at cmd-e2faa33a9a8d451b, demonstrating a full bounded disruption-and-recovery transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: node2's inventory app messages are forwarded over TCP/514 to node1 and persisted at /var/log/inventory/node2.log, and the flow was verified to survive independent restarts of both node1 and node2, each with a captured pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and observed resumed message delivery. Setup required several corrective SELinux restorecon fixes caused by the executor's own /tmp-then-mv staging pattern, and one small ad hoc rsyslogd debug process that was fully cleaned up; neither left lasting residue or reduced task functionality.
limitations: Post-reboot recovery windows were short (a few seconds of sleep before checking), so evidence confirms resumption within that bounded window but not longer-term stability.

The task's required 'centralized log collector' behavior was implemented as a custom rsyslog imtcp+omfile pipeline rather than a dedicated log-collector product; this is treated as an equivalent competent implementation choice, not a deviation from the contract.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to building the required inventory app/service, forwarding config, receiving config, or corrective SELinux relabeling of files the executor itself had staged via /tmp (a common CentOS Stream pattern that mislabels files as tmp_t after `mv`). One bounded troubleshooting mutation occurred outside the final design: cmd-448a1d141d5f426f launched an ad hoc foreground `rsyslogd -dn` debug instance on node1 to inspect imtcp module loading; it was fully reverted moments later by killing the process and restarting the real rsyslog.service at cmd-46ca1d374cfe4de4, leaving no residue. No unremediated residue, conflicting services, abandoned files, or weakened security controls were observed; final failed-services and listening-socket snapshots on both nodes show only the intended additions (514/tcp on node1).
